The man said "No, I don't care. Leave it alone and get away from it." John said "Please help the bird. It needs my help." The man replied, "No, it's not worth my time. Leave it and go away!" John sadly looked at the bird. He wished he could help it. He smiled and went away. The little bird died soon after, alone in the pile of ash with no help. John looked back and smiled sadly. He knew that he should have kept trying harder to help.

He climbed up the tree and reached for the hive. Suddenly, the bees appeared and started to sting him. Benny ran away as fast as he could, but he was too slow because of his big waist. He got stung all over and felt very sad. The next day, Benny went back to the beehive with a plan. He brought a big pot of honey and left it next to the hive. The bees smelled the honey and went to investigate. While they were distracted, Benny took some honey from the hive and ran away. He was very happy and learned that sometimes it's better to be patient and not take risks.
Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the woods. They found a big pile of lumber that someone left behind. They decided to own it and build a fort with it. "Look at all this lumber!" Tom said. "We can make a great fort with it!" "Yes, let's own it and build it here!" Sam agreed. "No one else can have it!" They worked hard and made a fort with the lumber. They put a sign on it that said "Tom and Sam's Fort. Keep Out!" They were very proud of their fort. One day, a man came to the woods. He was looking for his lumber that he lost. He saw the fort and the sign. He was very angry. "Hey, you kids!" he shouted. "This is my lumber! You stole it from me!" Tom and Sam were scared. They ran out of the fort and tried to explain. "No, we didn't steal it!" Tom said. "We found it here! We didn't know it was yours!" "Too bad!" the man said. "You should have asked before you took it! Now I'm taking it back!" He tore down the fort and took the lumber away. Tom and Sam were left with nothing but an empty space. They cried and wished they had been more careful. The moral of the story is: Don't take what is not yours. Always ask before you own something.

They tell Sara and Ben that they can still have plans, but not silly ones. They tell Sara and Ben that they can still dream, but not forget reality. Sara and Ben nod. They hug Mama and Papa and the elephant. They are happy and grateful. They have learned a lesson. They still love to play, but they play more wisely. They still love the elephant, but they love it more gently. They still have plans, but they plan more safely.

He had seen a firework once before, when he was very little. He remembered how it made him jump and cover his ears. He also remembered how it made him smile and clap his hands. He hoped Lily would like it too. They spread a big blanket on the grass and sat down. Mom gave them each a cup of hot chocolate and a cookie. Dad checked his watch and said, "It's almost time. All the people around the machine began to smile and dance to the music. The machine even started to dance! It was so excited! The people danced and sang with the machine until the rain stopped pouring. Then the machine said goodbye and went back to being lazy. But every time it rained, the machine remembered the happy feeling and turned on again.

Tim and Anna were twins who lived on a farm with their mom and dad. They liked to play outside and see the animals. One day, they saw a big truck with many sheep inside. The truck stopped near their house and the driver opened the door. "Hello, kids. I'm Mr. Lee. I'm here to shear the sheep. Do you know what that means?" he asked. Tim and Anna shook their heads. They did not know what shear meant. "It means I cut the wool from the sheep. The wool is very useful. We can make clothes and blankets and rugs from it. Do you want to see how I do it?" he said. Tim and Anna nodded. They wanted to see how he did it. They followed him to a big shed where he took out a sheep from the truck. The sheep was white and fluffy and made a baa sound. Mr. Lee put the sheep on a table and turned on a machine. The machine had a sharp blade that moved very fast. He moved the blade over the sheep and the wool came off. The sheep looked smaller and pinker without the wool. "Wow, that's amazing!" Tim said. "Does it hurt the sheep?" Anna asked. "No, it doesn't hurt the sheep. It's like getting a haircut. The sheep feel cooler and lighter after they are sheared. And they grow new wool every year. See, I put the wool in a big bag. I will take it to the factory where they will wash it and spin it and dye it and make it into useful things," Mr. Lee said. Tim and Anna touched the wool. It was soft and warm. They wondered how it could turn into clothes and blankets and rugs. They thanked Mr. Lee for showing them how he sheared the sheep. They learned something new and useful that day.

He wanted to see them stay safe, too. So with one big breath, he made all the ducks freeze. He smiled and watched them. The man kept walking until he saw a little girl. He wanted to make sure she was safe too. So with a huge breath, he made the little girl freeze. But then the sun came out and everything became warm. All the things the man froze started to move again. The flower, the ducks, and the little girl all shook off the cold and started to play and have fun. The man was very happy to see this, and never froze anything again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Benny. Benny loved to eat berries. One day, Benny went to the forest to find some berries to eat. The eagle replied, "No, these are my berries. I found them first." Benny said, "But I value those berries so much. I am so hungry and they look so yummy." The eagle thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, you can have some of the berries. But only if you promise to share with me." Benny happily agreed and they both ate the berries together. They became friends and went on many more berry-picking adventures together. The end.

It said there was a dance show in the town hall. Sara asked her mom if they could go. Her mom said yes, but they had to hurry. They got on the bus and went to the town hall. Sara was very excited. They found their seats and waited for the show to start. Sara saw a big stage with lights and curtains. She saw many people in the audience. She saw some dancers backstage, warming up and stretching. She wished she could be one of them. The show began. Sara watched the dancers with wide eyes. They moved with grace and skill. They jumped and spun and smiled. They wore colorful dresses and shoes. Sara clapped and cheered for them. She wanted to dance like them. At the end of the show, the dancers came to the front of the stage and bowed. The audience gave them a big applause. Sara saw one dancer who looked like the one in her book. She was the star of the show. She had long hair and a pink dress. Sara thought she was the most beautiful dancer in the world. Sara wanted to meet her. She asked her mom if they could go backstage. Her mom said no, they had to go home. Sara was sad. She wanted to talk to the dancer and tell her how much she liked her. She wanted to ask her how she became a dancer. She wanted to touch her dress and shoes. Sara did not give up. She waited until her mom was not looking. She got up from her seat and ran to the stage. She climbed the stairs and reached the curtain. She peeked behind it and saw the dancer. She was sitting on a chair, taking off her shoes. She looked tired and happy. Sara walked towards her. She wanted to say hello. But before she could, she heard her mom's voice. Her mom had seen her and followed her. Her mom was angry. She grabbed Sara's hand and pulled her away. She scolded Sara for running away and being rude. Sara cried. She did not mean to be rude. She just wanted to meet the dancer. She looked back at the curtain and saw the dancer looking at her. The dancer smiled and waved. She said something to Sara, but Sara could not hear her. She wondered what she said. The dancer said, "You are a brave and curious girl. You remind me of myself when I was your age. I also loved to dance and wanted to meet dancers. I also ran away from my mom once to see a show. Don't be sad. Don't be afraid. Keep dancing. Maybe one day, you will be a dancer too. And maybe one day, I will see you on the stage. You have a humble and kind heart. That is the most important thing for a dancer. Goodbye, little one. I hope we meet again."

"I can help you," said the big bird. The big bird used its long legs to stretch and get the red ball. The big bird gave the red ball to the brown bunny. The brown bunny was very happy. "Thank you, big bird," said the brown bunny. They played with the red ball together near the big bush all day.

Lily was still sad, but then she saw the beautiful sunset. She said, "Look, Mommy! The sunset is so pretty!" Her mom said, "Yes, it is." Lily forgot about the puppy and enjoyed the sunset with her mom. They went home happy and had dinner together. The end.
Lily and Ben were making cookies with Mom. They liked to stir the dough and cut out shapes with the cookie cutters. Mom said they could decorate the cookies with sprinkles and candy. Lily saw a shiny ornament on the tree. It was red and round and had glitter on it. She wanted to put it on her cookie. She reached for the ornament and pulled it off the branch. "Hey, what are you doing?" Ben asked. He saw Lily holding the ornament in her hand. "I want to put this on my cookie. It is pretty," Lily said. "That is not for cookies. That is for the tree. It is not food. It is glass. You are stupid," Ben said. Lily felt angry. She did not like Ben calling her stupid. She threw the ornament at Ben. It missed him and hit the wall. It broke into pieces. Mom heard the noise and came into the kitchen. She saw the broken ornament and the mess on the floor. She was not happy. "Lily, Ben, what happened here?" Mom asked. Lily and Ben looked at each other. They did not know what to say. They felt sorry. They knew they did something bad.

He is black and dirty. He barks at the snowman. He runs to the snowman and bites his hat. He pulls his scarf. He knocks down the coal. The snowman looks sad. "Stop, dog! Stop!" Sam and Tom shout. They throw snowballs at the dog. The dog is scared. He runs away. Sam and Tom look at the snowman. He is not big anymore. He is not happy anymore. He is dirty and broken. Sam and Tom are sad. They hug the snowman. They say, "We are sorry, snowman. We love you." They stretch their arms and pick up the coal. They put it back on the snowman's face. They find a new hat and a new scarf. They make the snowman big and happy again. They smile at the snowman. The snowman smiles back. They are happy again.
Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with trains. They had a big box of trains and tracks that they could make different shapes with. They also had a station where the trains could stop and go. One day, they saw a new train set in the toy store. It was shiny and colorful and had a lot of cars and bridges. It also had a station that could make sounds and lights. Tom and Lily wanted the new train set very much. They asked their mom if they could have it. "Mom, can we have the new train set? It is so pretty and fun!" they said. Mom looked at the price tag and shook her head. "No, my dears, we cannot buy the new train set. It is too expensive. We have to save our money for other things. You already have a nice train set at home. Why don't you play with that?" Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They did not want to play with their old train set. They thought it was boring and ugly. They threw a tantrum and cried and shouted. Mom was upset and disappointed. She took them home and sent them to their room. Tom and Lily sat on their bed and sulked. They did not talk to each other or to mom. They wished they had the new train set. They did not think about how mom worked hard to buy them things they needed. They did not think about how lucky they were to have a train set at all. After a while, they heard a knock on the door. It was their friend Ben. He had a big smile on his face and a small bag in his hand. "Hi, Tom and Lily! I have a surprise for you!" he said. He opened the bag and took out a small train. It was not shiny or colorful. It was made of wood and had no cars or bridges. It had a name on it: Ben. "Look, this is my train. I made it myself with my dad. He helped me cut the wood and paint it. It is not fancy, but it is special. It is my train and it has my name on it. Do you want to play with it?" he asked. Tom and Lily looked at Ben's train. They felt ashamed of their tantrum. They realized that Ben was happy with his simple train. He did not need a new train set. He was proud of his train and he wanted to share it with them. He was a good friend. They smiled and said, "Yes, Ben, we want to play with your train. Thank you for bringing it. It is a nice train and it has your name on it. We are sorry we were rude and greedy. We have a train set too. It is not new, but it is ours. We can make a big track and have a lot of fun. Come on, let's go to our station!" They hugged Ben and ran to their station. They took out their trains and tracks and started to play. They made a big circle and put Ben's train in the middle. They pretended that Ben's train was the leader and their trains were the followers. They made sounds and lights with their mouths and hands. They laughed and had a blast. Mom heard them and smiled. She was glad that they learned their lesson. She thought, "It is not the price of the toy that matters, but the joy of playing with it. It is not the look of the train that counts, but the name of the friend who shares it."

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They saw a big sign that said "Zoo". They wanted to see the animals, so they asked their mom if they could go. "OK, but we have to be careful and stay together," mom said. "The zoo has many different animals, some are friendly and some are not." They walked to the zoo and bought tickets. They saw monkeys, birds, elephants, and giraffes. They learned their names and sounds. They had fun feeding the goats and petting the rabbits. Then they came to a big cage with a sign that said "Tiger". They saw a big orange and black animal with sharp teeth and claws. It was lying on a rock and licking its paw. "Wow, look at that tiger!" Ben said. "It is so big and strong!" "I don't like it," Anna said. "It is scary and mean!" "No, it is not," Ben said. "It is just an animal. It can't hurt us. We are safe behind the fence." He wanted to get a closer look, so he walked to the fence and waved his hand. "Hello, tiger!" he said. The tiger heard him and opened its eyes. It saw Ben and growled. It jumped off the rock and ran to the fence. It roared and showed its teeth. Ben was frightened. He screamed and ran back to mom and Anna. The tiger hit the fence with its paw and made a loud noise. Mom hugged Ben and Anna and calmed them down. "It's OK, it's OK," she said. "The tiger can't get out. It was just curious and wanted to see you. But you should never tease or bother the animals. They might get angry or scared." "I'm sorry, mom," Ben said. "I didn't mean to make the tiger mad. I just wanted to say hi." "I know, honey," mom said. "But you have to be respectful and careful. The animals are not toys. They have feelings and needs. You have to learn how to treat them well." Anna and Ben nodded. They said sorry to the tiger and left the cage. They decided to see some other animals that were more friendly and gentle. They learned a lot at the zoo and had a good time.

Lily was a little rabbit who liked to hop and play in the meadow. She had many friends, like Daisy the mouse and Sam the squirrel. One day, she saw a new animal in the grass. It was brown and furry, with long ears and a fluffy tail. Lily was curious and wanted to say hello. "Hello, I am Lily," she said to the new animal. "Who are you?" "Hello, I am Ben," the new animal said. "I am a hare. I just moved here from the forest." Lily smiled and said, "You look like me, but bigger and faster. Do you want to play with me and my friends?" Ben nodded and said, "Yes, I would like that. Thank you for being nice to me." Lily and Ben hopped to the other side of the meadow, where Daisy and Sam were waiting. Lily introduced Ben to them and they all became friends. They played tag and hide and seek and had a lot of fun. But they did not notice that a hunter was watching them from behind a bush. He had a gun and a net and wanted to catch them. He was very quiet and sneaky and waited for the right moment to attack. Suddenly, he jumped out of the bush and aimed his gun at Ben. He pulled the trigger and a loud bang echoed in the air. Lily, Daisy and Sam were scared and ran away as fast as they could. But Ben was not so lucky. He was hit by the bullet and fell to the ground. He was hurt and bleeding and could not move. Lily saw what happened and felt very sad and angry. She wanted to help Ben, but she knew it was too dangerous. She wished she could do something to stop the hunter. She looked around and saw a big rock near the bush. She had an idea. She ran to the rock and pushed it with all her strength. The rock rolled down the hill and hit the hunter on the head. He dropped his gun and net and fell to the ground. He was knocked out and could not hurt anyone anymore. Lily ran back to Ben and hugged him. She hoped he would be okay. She said, "You are my friend, Ben. I am sorry this happened to you. You are brave and strong and I love you." Ben smiled weakly and said, "You are my friend, too, Lily. You are smart and kind and I love you. Thank you for saving me. You are a hero." Lily and Ben cuddled together and waited for help. Soon, Daisy and Sam came back with some other animals. They brought some leaves and flowers to heal Ben's wound. They also brought some carrots and nuts to cheer him up. They all surrounded Lily and Ben and thanked them for being their friends. They were happy and safe and free.

Suddenly, she saw a strange bee flying around in a crazy way and making a loud noise. Buffy: "Hi! What's your name?" Crazy Bee: "My name is Zazz and I'm on a mission to find the sweetest honey in the world." Buffy: "That sounds cool! Can I join you?" Crazy Bee: "Sure, come with me!" So they flew around looking for the sweetest honey ever. After a while, they found the sweetest honey and it was right in Buffy's own hive! Buffy: "Wow, I never knew the sweetest honey was right in my own hive!" Zazz: "Yes, sometimes the best things are right under our noses. It's important to take a break from our daily routine and explore to find new things." The moral of this story is that it's important to take some time to explore and experience new things. So next time, don't forget to take a break and stir things up a bit!

Unfortunately, as soon as Lily touched it, the flower withered away. Lily was very upset and started to cry. Her mom said,'Now you see, Lily. You don't always need what you want.' Lily understood that this was her lesson and never picked a flower again.

Tom and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the snow and make snowmen. One day, they saw a big hill with lots of snow. They wanted to slide down the hill on their sleds. "Let's go, Lily! It will be fun!" Tom said. "OK, Tom. But promise me we will be careful. The hill is very steep and fast." Lily said. "I promise, Lily. Don't worry. We will be safe." Tom said. They took their sleds and climbed up the hill. They were very excited. They looked at the view. It was brilliant. They could see the whole town and the sun shining. "Ready, Lily?" Tom asked. "Ready, Tom!" Lily answered. They pushed their sleds and started to slide down the hill. They laughed and screamed. They felt the wind and the snow on their faces. They were having so much fun. But then, something bad happened. Tom's sled hit a rock and flipped over. Tom fell off his sled and rolled down the hill. He hit a tree and hurt his head. He cried and cried. Lily saw what happened and stopped her sled. She ran to Tom and hugged him. "Tom, Tom, are you OK? I'm so sorry. I'm here for you." Lily said. Tom looked at Lily with tears in his eyes. "Lily, you promised me we would be careful. You lied to me. You made me crash. You are not my friend anymore." Tom said. Lily felt very sad and sorry. She tried to say something, but Tom did not listen. He pushed her away and ran to his home. Lily was left alone on the hill. She wished she could take back her promise. She wished she could make Tom happy again. She wished they could have cocoa and cookies together. But it was too late. The moral of the story is: Don't make promises you can't keep. They can hurt your friends and yourself. Be honest and responsible.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toys. But they did not like to share. They always fought over who got the best toy or the most toys. One day, they were playing with their cars and trucks. Ben wanted the red truck, but Sam had it. Sam wanted the blue car, but Ben had it. "Give me the red truck!" Ben shouted. "No, it's mine!" Sam shouted back. "Give me the blue car!" Ben shouted again. "No, it's mine!" Sam shouted again. They pulled and pushed and yelled at each other. They did not listen to their mom, who told them to stop fighting and play nicely. They did not care about the law, which said that they had to respect each other and their things. They were very angry and selfish. Then, they heard a loud noise. It was their dad, who came home from work. He saw them fighting and was very upset. He took away all their toys and put them in a box. "What are you doing?" Ben and Sam cried. "You are not playing with your toys. You are fighting with them. You are breaking the law of our house, which says that you have to share and be kind. You are making me and your mom very sad. You have to surrender your toys until you learn how to play nicely." Dad said. Ben and Sam felt very sorry. They realized that they had been very bad. They did not want to lose their toys. They did not want to make their dad and mom sad. They wanted to be good brothers. "Please, dad, can we have our toys back?" Ben and Sam asked. "Only if you promise to share and be kind. And you have to say sorry to each other and hug." Dad said. Ben and Sam nodded. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They said sorry to their dad and mom and hugged them too. They promised to share and be kind. Dad gave them back their toys and smiled. "Good boys. I'm proud of you. Now you can play with your toys. But remember, the law of our house is to share and be kind. And if you don't, you have to surrender your toys again." Dad said. Ben and Sam understood. They thanked their dad and mom and played with their toys. They took turns with the red truck and the blue car. They did not fight anymore. They were happy and peaceful. The moral of the story is: It is better to share and be kind than to fight and be angry. If you break the law, you have to surrender what you love. If you follow the law, you can keep what you love and make others happy too.

The match was very excited, and they started to practice every day. The sun would rise, and the match would try to rise too. But the match could not rise like the sun. Then one day, the sun had an idea. It told the match, "You may not rise in the sky like me, but you can rise in another way." The sun helped the match to stand up tall and strong. The match felt very happy and proud. From that day on, the match knew that it could rise in its own special way, and it continued to bring light and warmth to everyone.
Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the forest near their home. They liked to run, jump, climb and explore. One day, they saw a big lake with ice on it. They wanted to slide on the ice and have fun. "Come on, Ben, let's go on the ice!" Lily said. "No, Lily, we can't. Mom said it is not safe. The ice can break and we can fall in the water. It is very cold and we can get sick or hurt." Ben said. "But it looks so fun! And it is very quiet here. No one will see us or hear us. Please, Ben, just for a little bit." Lily said. Lily did not listen to Ben and ran to the ice. She started to slide and laugh. Ben followed her, because he did not want to leave her alone. They slid and laughed for a while, until they heard a loud crack. The ice was breaking under their feet. They were scared and tried to run back to the shore, but it was too late. They fell in the water and felt the cold. "Help! Help!" they cried. Luckily, a man who was walking his dog heard their cries and came to help them. He threw a rope to them and pulled them out of the water. He wrapped them in a blanket and took them to his car. He drove them to their home and told their mom what happened. Mom was very angry and worried. She hugged them and thanked the man. She took them inside and gave them warm clothes and soup. She also gave them a big lecture. "Lily and Ben, you were very naughty and foolish. You did not listen to me or to each other. You went on the ice without permission and put yourselves in danger. You could have died or got very sick. You must never do that again. Do you understand?" Mom said. "Yes, Mom, we understand. We are very sorry. We will never do that again. We love you, Mom." Lily and Ben said. Mom smiled and kissed them. She was glad they were safe and learned their lesson. The moral of the story is: listen to your parents and your siblings. They know what is best for you and want to protect you. Do not go on the ice without permission. It is not safe and not fun. It is dangerous and scary.
Tom was a bald boy who liked to play with fire. He had a box of matches that he hid under his bed. One day, he saw a parade on the street. He wanted to join the fun, so he took his matches and ran outside. He saw a big float with a dragon on it. The dragon had a long tail and shiny scales. Tom thought it would be funny to make the dragon spit fire. He lit a match and threw it at the dragon's mouth. But he missed and hit the float instead. The float caught fire and started to burn. The people on the float screamed and jumped off. The fire spread to the other floats and the street. The parade turned into a panic. Tom was scared and ran back to his house. But he did not know that he dropped his matches on the way. The matches also caught fire and burned a trail to his house. The fire reached his bed and burned his box of matches. The fire also burned his toys, his clothes and his books. Tom's house was on fire. Tom's mom and dad smelled the smoke and ran to his room. They saw Tom crying and the fire everywhere. They grabbed Tom and ran outside. They called the firemen to put out the fire. Tom's mom and dad were very angry and sad. They asked Tom why he did such a bad thing. Tom said he was sorry and he did not mean to burn the parade and his house. He said he just wanted to play with fire and make the dragon spit fire. He said he liked fire because it was bright and warm. Tom's mom and dad told him that fire was not a toy. They told him that fire was dangerous and could hurt people and things. They told him that he should never play with fire or matches again. They told him that he should be careful and respectful of other people's things. They told him that he should be thankful that he and his family were safe. Tom learned his lesson. He felt very sorry for what he did. He said he would never play with fire or matches again. He said he would be a good boy and help his mom and dad rebuild their house. He said he would also apologize to the people in the parade and help them fix their floats. He said he would be more careful and respectful of other people's things. He said he would be thankful for what he had. The moral of the story is: Do not play with fire or matches. Fire is dangerous and can hurt people and things. Be careful and respectful of other people's things. Be thankful for what you have.

They put on the black clothes and the black hat and the black veil and the black necklace. They look at each other and laugh. They look very different. They take the black book and go downstairs. They see their mom in the kitchen. She is making cookies. She sees them and smiles. She says, "Wow, you look very nice. Where are you going?" Lila says, "We are going to a temple, mom." Sam says, "Yes, a temple. Do you know what it is?" Mom says, "A temple is a place where people go to pray and worship. It can be for different religions and cultures. Your grandma used to go to a temple when she was young. She was a Jewish woman. That's why she had these clothes and this book. They are part of her tradition and faith." Lila and Sam are curious. They ask, "What is Jewish? What is tradition? What is faith?" Mom says, "Those are big words, but they mean something important. Jewish is a group of people who share a history and a belief in God. Tradition is a way of doing things that has been passed down from generation to generation. Faith is a feeling of trust and love for God and for others. Your grandma had all of these things, and she wanted you to know about them too. That's why she left you this box." Lila and Sam are amazed. They say, "Wow, grandma was very special. We want to know more about her and her temple." Mom says, "That's wonderful. I can tell you more stories and show you more pictures. Maybe one day, we can even visit a temple together. But first, how about some cookies?" Lila and Sam say, "Yes, please!" They hug their mom and thank her. They are happy to learn about their grandma and her temple. They are happy to wear her clothes and her hat and her veil and her necklace and her book. They are happy to play dress-up. They are happy to be friends.

Once upon a time there was a monkey who loved to eat delicious fruit. One day he stumbled upon a vine growing alongside a tall cliff. The vine had such delicious fruit that the monkey could not resist. He shimmied up the vine and began to pick the yummy fruit. Just as he was reaching for the most delicious looking fruit, an eagle suddenly appeared in the sky. It flew right at the monkey and tried to peck him! The monkey quickly grabbed onto the vine and tried to avoid the eagle's claws. The monkey was in trouble. He was too high up the vine for the eagle to reach, but the vine was becoming weak from the monkey's weight. In a desperate move to get away, the monkey quickly released its grip and jumped off the vine. The monkey's plan worked and he rose high into the sky, high enough to escape the eagleâ€™s claws. As the eagle watched in disbelief, the monkey flew off with the delicious fruit and never looked back.
Once upon a time, there was a scared little rabbit. He was very frightened and didn't know what to do. He was alone in the forest, and he started to cry. Just then, a friendly little bird flew over to him. The bird said, "What is wrong, little rabbit?" The rabbit said he was scared, and the bird said, "Don't worry, I'll comfort you." The bird said she would give the rabbit a crown and make him feel better. She put the crown on the rabbit's head, and the rabbit stopped crying. The bird said, "There, now things don't seem as frightening, do they?" The rabbit nodded and smiled. He thanked the bird and said, "Let's go explore the forest together!" The bird and the rabbit then went off on a big adventure, their crowns shining brightly in the daylight.
Once upon a time, there was a big, hard birdcage. Inside the birdcage lived a happy bird who wanted to get out but the cage was very hard and the bird could not get out. The bird demanded that the cage be opened, but the people around him could not understand what he was saying. Then, one day, a kind little girl who was only three years old came along. The bird saw the girl, and he began to demand again that the cage be opened. This time, the little girl understood! She got a long piece of rope and started to pull the birdcage until it opened up. The bird was so excited to be let out. The little girl and the bird became good friends. She would come to see the bird every day, and they would play together. The bird was so happy to be able to fly around and explore the world outside the cage. The bird was grateful to the little girl for understanding his demands and helping him out of the hard birdcage.
Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big sandbox where they could make castles and dig holes. Sometimes they also played with their dog, Spot, who was very friendly and fluffy. One day, their mom told them to behave and not to make a mess, because they had to go to a party later. She gave them each a pink cupcake and a glass of milk, and said she would be back soon. Lily and Ben said thank you and promised to be good. But after they ate their cupcakes, they saw that Spot had jumped into the sandbox and was digging up the soil. He was having fun, but he was also making a big mess. He had soil all over his fur and his paws, and he was throwing it everywhere. "Spot, stop it!" Lily shouted. "You are making a mess! Mom will be angry!" But Spot did not listen. He wagged his tail and barked happily. He ran towards Lily and Ben, and tried to lick their faces. "Yuck!" Ben said. "Spot, you are dirty! Go away!" But Spot did not go away. He jumped on them and knocked them over. He rolled them in the soil and the sand, and made them dirty too. He thought it was a game, and he was having fun. Lily and Ben tried to push him off, but he was too strong. They started to cry. They did not like being dirty. They wanted to be clean and pretty for the party. "Help!" they cried. "Mom, help!" Their mom heard them and came running. She saw the mess and was shocked. She saw Spot and was angry. She saw Lily and Ben and was sad. "What happened here?" she asked. "Did you behave?" Lily and Ben shook their heads. They felt sorry. They knew they had broken their promise. "We are sorry, mom," they said. "Spot did it. He was naughty. He made us dirty." Their mom sighed. She was not happy, but she was not mean. She loved them, and she knew they were kids. "Come on," she said. "Let's go inside and clean up. Maybe we can still make it to the party. But next time, you have to behave. And Spot, you too. No more digging in the sandbox, okay?" Spot wagged his tail and barked. He did not understand what she said, but he knew she was not mad. He followed them inside, hoping for another cupcake. He liked cupcakes. They were pink and sweet.
One day, Anna and Ben went to the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They also liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. "Look, Anna, a bee!" Ben said, pointing to a yellow and black insect on a daisy. "It is making honey!" Anna nodded. She liked honey on her toast. She wanted to see the bee closer. She walked to the flower and leaned in. "Be careful, Anna," mom said. "Bees can sting you if they feel scared. They don't like it when you touch them." Anna did not listen. She reached out her hand to touch the bee. But the bee did not like that. It flew up and buzzed angrily. Then it stung Anna on her finger. "Ow!" Anna cried. She ran back to mom, holding her finger. "It hurts, mom, it hurts!" Mom hugged Anna and looked at her finger. She saw a little red bump. She took out a band-aid from her bag and put it on Anna's finger. "It's okay, Anna," mom said. "The bee was just trying to protect itself. It did not mean to hurt you. You have to be compassionate to the bees. They are important for the flowers and the honey." Anna sniffed. She looked at the bee, still on the daisy. She felt sorry for the bee. She did not want to hurt it either. "I'm sorry, bee," Anna said. "I won't touch you again. You can make honey and be happy." The bee seemed to notice Anna's words. It flew away from the flower and buzzed around Anna's head. Then it landed on her band-aid and rubbed its legs. It was like saying thank you. Anna smiled. She felt better. She learned to be compassionate to the bees. She and Ben went back to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They had a fun day at the park.
